display.purpose: Hero headlines and brand wordmark only. Fraunces italic for evocative phrases; upright for declarative payoffs.

price.purpose: Current price figure on album cards. The most-scanned data point per screen. Tabular numerals.

title.purpose: Album title on cards. Fraunces at small scale for warmth. Line-clamped to 2 lines.

body.purpose: Guide prose, descriptions, about pages. DM Sans, max 65-75ch line length for prose contexts.

label.purpose: Artist names, filter/sort eyebrows, footer section headers. Uppercase, tracked, ≤4 words.

caption.purpose: Metadata, timestamps, status text, affiliate disclaimers. Dust color minimum.

shadows.name: cut-badge
shadows.purpose: Cut Red discount badge — separates it from dark album art.

shadows.name: focus-gold
shadows.purpose: Focus ring on inputs, buttons, chips. Applied via box-shadow, not outline.

shadows.name: deal-ring
shadows.purpose: Tier-3 deal card ring. Applied at rest to signal best-price status.

motion.name: vinyl-pulse
motion.purpose: Loading skeleton pulse. Stopped under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: nav-progress
motion.purpose: Router navigation progress indicator at top of viewport.

motion.name: hover-scale
motion.purpose: Album art scale on card hover. Signals interactivity.

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Default transition for all interactive components.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Mobile/tablet split. Nav collapses below; search goes full-width below.

narrative.overview:
Garimpa Vinil runs on the obsessive energy of flicking through record sleeves in a warm, dim shop — the kind where the owner knows every pressing and the last time a title dipped below R$80. The design doesn't simulate a streaming service or an e-commerce storefront. It simulates that shop: warm-dark surfaces, amber light catching the edge of a sleeve, deals surfaced with the quiet confidence of someone who has been watching prices for years.

The palette is the Den itself: near-black warm backgrounds layered from deep to slightly-less-deep, with amber gold as the single voice of action and value. Text lives on a warm cream-to-amber ramp, so every level of hierarchy reads as the same material, not a different page. Status signals (discount red, deal green) enter only when data warrants — never as decoration.

This system is built mobile-first for casual discovery, but its density and precision serve the obsessive collector equally. The deal is always the hero. Fraunces carries display headings, album titles, and price figures: wherever the data is the content. DM Sans handles everything else without asking to be noticed.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-dark tonal layering without drop shadows; depth through surface steps (Record → Sleeve → Label → Groove → Wax)
Gold accent reserved for primary action and deal signal only; its scarcity is what makes deals visible
Fraunces for display, album titles, and prices; DM Sans for all UI chrome — never mixed
Touch-native density: readable at arm's length, tappable at 44px minimum
Grain overlay at 3.5% opacity across the body; vinyl-groove radial decoration on hero surfaces
Motion is functional: state feedback and page transitions only; no orchestrated page-load choreography

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Gold (#d98f0e) is the only warm-bright accent in the entire system. It appears on primary buttons, active filter chips, current price figures, and the brand logo — nothing else. Its scarcity is what makes deals visible.

rules.name: The Depth-Without-Shadows Rule
rules.body: Visual depth is created by stepping through the neutral stack (Record → Sleeve → Label → Groove → Wax), not by drop shadows. Hover states shift the border one step warmer. Active states shift the background fill one level up.

rules.name: The Dust Floor Rule
rules.body: Dust (#957060) is the lightest permissible text color on dark surfaces. It is the system's WCAG AA floor. Below it — lighter, more muted — text fails contrast and is prohibited.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows on cards, modals, drawers, or containers at rest. Before reaching for box-shadow, ask whether a border-color shift or background-fill step does the job. It almost always does.

rules.name: The Fraunces Reservation Rule
rules.body: Fraunces appears in exactly three contexts: display/hero headings, album titles on cards, and current price figures. It is prohibited in navigation, buttons, labels, captions, form controls, filter chips, sort selects, or any UI chrome.

rules.name: The Uppercase Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Uppercase text is reserved for: artist name labels (≤4 words, tracked at 0.2em), filter/sort label eyebrows (≤4 words), and deal badge text. Never uppercase for body copy, album titles, or headings.

dos: Do use Gold (#d98f0e) exclusively for primary actions, active states, current prices, and the brand logo.
Do express depth through tonal surface steps (Record → Sleeve → Label → Groove → Wax). Step the border one stop warmer on hover; step the background fill one level up on active.
Do use Fraunces for hero headings, album titles, and price figures only. DM Sans handles every other text role.
Do ensure minimum text contrast: Dust (#957060) on Record Black (#0c0a08) is the WCAG AA floor at 4.5:1.
Do size all tap targets to minimum 44px height for mobile-first touch use.
Do include @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) alternatives for every animation.
Do use text-wrap: balance on h1–h3 and text-wrap: pretty on prose paragraphs in guide content.
Do gate all deal badges and price-history features behind NEXT_PUBLIC_HIDE_PRICE_HISTORY.
donts: Don't use Gold as a decorative highlight, section divider tint, or background wash. The One Voice Rule.
Don't use Fraunces in navigation, buttons, filter chips, form controls, labels, or any UI chrome.
Don't add drop shadows to cards, containers, or layout surfaces. The Flat-By-Default Rule.
Don't make this look like a SaaS product: no hero metrics, no purple/blue/teal brand colors, no feature-grid layouts.
Don't make this look like a streaming service: no Spotify green, no Apple Music pink, no playlist-card visual language.
Don't make this look like an e-commerce giant: no Amazon/Mercado Livre blue-and-orange, no Add-to-Cart language.
Don't use border-left greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards or callouts.
Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient fill. Gold is always solid.
Don't use glassmorphism decoratively. Backdrop blur is reserved for the sticky navbar and mobile overlay.
Don't add orchestrated page-load motion sequences. State-change feedback and page transitions only.
Don't use text lighter than Dust (#957060) on dark surfaces. The Dust Floor Rule.
Don't show deal badges or discount percentages when NEXT_PUBLIC_HIDE_PRICE_HISTORY is true.
